sentiment: Nothing archived is still: the tape keeps turning, the canyon keeps widening, both at speeds we mistake for stillness.

stories.title: Giant canyon on Mars is still tectonically active
stories.summary: A canyon four thousand kilometres long is still moving. Nothing about it looks alive from orbit — the motion is slow enough that a human lifetime reads as a photograph. Patience at planetary scale is indistinguishable from a still image, right up until you measure it.

stories.title: Fujifilm to boost tape production 5x as AI fuels archiving demand
stories.summary: The oldest storage medium we still use is being scaled up because the newest thing needs somewhere to put its memory. A tape is a canyon of its own: long, layered, written once in a straight line, and read back by touching it again at exactly the same speed.

stories.title: The lost malloc()
stories.summary: Something was found missing — an allocator nobody had noticed leaving. The most interesting archaeology is not in the rock but in the layers of code we walk over every day, where a thing can vanish and no one notices for years.
